contents.name: (6.20)-(6.35) printed pp. 145-149: the weak-field decomposition g = eta + h, gauge transformations, harmonic (de Donder) gauge and the linearized field equations
contents.support: The theorem derives the linearized equation as the first-order consequence of the adopted field law along a family of solutions, which strengthens the source's fixed-background linearization; the source supplies the linearized equation, the gauge transformation law and the harmonic-gauge reduction.

contents.name: (6.30)-(6.44) printed pp. 148-150: plane-wave solutions hbar = C e^{ikx}, the null wavevector condition, transversality and the trace-reversed form
contents.support: The definition turns the source's ansatz into an exact local definition of planar perturbations, single-frequency plane waves, trace-reversed amplitudes and the harmonic-gauge condition, with an explicit scope clause that asserts no existence.

contents.name: (6.39)-(6.53) printed pp. 149-151: the gauge transformation converting a harmonic-gauge plane wave to transverse-traceless form with the explicit coefficients B_mu
contents.support: The lemma proves the exact decomposition V_0 = T direct-sum G with a unique TT representative and the explicit triangular system for Z, absorbing the source's coefficient list; the worked instance is ex-gr-plane-wave-regauge-to-tt.

contents.name: (6.55)-(6.57) printed pp. 151-152: the projector P = eta - n n and the transverse-traceless projection with the half-trace subtraction
contents.support: The definition fixes the screen projector of rank two on the observer rest space and the TT projection, and lem-gr-tt-screen-projector proves idempotence, ranks and orthogonality; the rank-three variant of the half-trace formula is refuted by cex-gr-half-trace-subtraction-on-the-rest-space.

contents.name: (6.58)-(6.66) printed pp. 152-153: the geodesic deviation equation for slowly moving test particles, R^i_{00j} = (1/2) d_0^2 h^i_j and the oscillating separations for the two polarizations
contents.support: The response theorem derives the exact deviation equation for the straight free-fall family, its first-order expansion and the ideal-detector strain from the clock and free-fall postulates; the source's component formula R^i_{00j} is recovered as clause (b) and checked in step 3.2. The explicit sinusoidal instance is ex-gr-sinusoidal-tt-plane-wave.

contents.name: 5.2.1 printed pp. 210-212: the plane-wave ansatz hbar_{mu nu} = Re(H_{mu nu} e^{ikx}), the null wavevector, transversality k^mu H_{mu nu} = 0 and the two polarisation states H_+ and H_x
contents.support: The definition records the ansatz, the null wave covector and the harmonic-gauge condition with exact smoothness hypotheses; the polarization classification at fixed k is the statement of pthm-gr-plane-wave-polarizations.

contents.name: 5.2.1 (5.20)-(5.22) printed pp. 211-212: the residual gauge transformation H -> H + i(k lambda + k lambda - k.rho lambda eta) and the transverse-traceless conditions restricted to the two-dimensional screen
contents.support: The lemma solves the residual gauge system in an adapted orthonormal frame and identifies the quotient V_0/G with the two-dimensional TT space; the screen conditions of the source are proved there rather than named.

contents.name: 5.2.2 printed pp. 212-216: the geodesic deviation equation d^2 S^mu/dt^2 = (1/2) d^2 h^mu_nu/dt^2 S^nu, the circle-to-ellipse deformation and the arm response L' = L(1 plus or minus H_+/2)
contents.support: The response theorem proves the deviation equation for the exact family, expands it in the amplitude and derives the strain; the ideal-detector model replaces the source's pictorial deformation by the precise proper-separation definition of def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling.

contents.support: The theorem proves that every pair of bounded smooth profiles gives a harmonic-gauge solution of the linearized vacuum equations and bounds the exact vacuum residual by a constant times the square of the amplitude on compact sets.

canonical.name: The conditional physical reading of the linearized waves: the field law derives the linearized equation, TT plane waves solve it up to a quadratic residual, the amplitude classification gives two polarizations, and the tidal response of ideal test bodies is a model deduction
canonical.support: The response theorem is the canonical derivation of the page's physical content: it establishes the free-fall worldlines, the exact deviation equation, its first-order expansion and the ideal-detector strain from the adopted clock and free-fall postulates, with the linearized residual of order lambda squared as the stated approximation. rem-gr-linearized-wave-scope-and-deferred records the exclusions.

contents.name: (6.53)-(6.57) printed pp. 151-152: the transverse-traceless amplitude matrix with components C_11, C_12 and the projector and half-trace subtraction
contents.support: The example projects an explicit symmetric tensor with the library's rank-two screen projector, computes the TT part and its amplitudes and verifies idempotence, providing a finite check of the projection definition against the source's formula.

contents.name: (6.55)-(6.57) printed pp. 151-152: the four-dimensional projector P = eta - n n and the half-trace subtraction
contents.support: The counterexample exhibits the failure of the half-trace subtraction with the rank-three spatial projector and contrasts it with the rank-two screen projection, delimiting the source formula's weight.

contents.name: (6.63)-(6.66) printed p. 153: the oscillating separations of nearby particles for the plus and cross polarizations
contents.support: The example computes the curvature components R^{(1)}_{0101} and R^{(1)}_{0102} of explicit sinusoidal profiles and the ideal-detector strain for arms along e_1 and (e_1+e_2)/sqrt2.

contents.name: (6.30)-(6.33) printed pp. 148-149: the plane-wave solution requires a null wave vector, so that the waves travel at the speed of light
contents.support: The counterexample shows quantitatively that a transverse-traceless planar profile travelling at speed 1/2 fails the linearized vacuum equations, with G^{(1)}_{11} = 3/4 != 0 at every point.
